'''''Fenestraria''''' (known as '''babies' toes''')<ref>{{citation |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=409580 |title=USDA GRIN Taxonomy |access-date=19 August 2016}}</ref> is a (possibly [[monotypic]]) genus of [[succulent plants]] in the family [[Aizoaceae]], native to the [[Namaqualand]] in [[Namibia]] and the [[Cape Provinces]] of South Africa.<ref name = powo/>

==Description==
[[Image:Fenestraria rhopalophylla.jpg|thumb|left|200px| ''F. rhopalophylla'' in flower]] 
[[Image:Fenestraria aurantica 1.jpg|thumb|left|200px|''F. rhopalophylla'' subsp. ''aurantica'']]
The only species currently recognised in this genus is '''''Fenestraria rhopalophylla'''''. 
Each leaf has an [[epidermal window]], a transparent window-like area, at its rounded tip, it is for these window-like structures that the genus is named (Latin: ''[[Window#Etymology|fenestra]]'').

''Fenestraria rhopalophylla'' appears very similar to ''[[Frithia pulchra]]'', though the leaves are a slightly different shape and ''F. rhopalophylla'' has yellow flowers, compared to the pink flowers of ''F. pulchra''.

==Distribution and habitat==
In the wild, the plant commonly grows under sand, except for the transparent tips, which allow light into the leaves for [[photosynthesis]]. 
The plant produces optical fibers made from crystalline [[oxalic acid]]<ref>{{citation |url=https://conservatory.cals.cornell.edu/2018/03/14/featured-plant-fenestraria-rhopalophylla-subsp-aurantiaca/ | title=Featured plant: Fenestraria rhopalophylla subsp. aurantiaca |access-date=25 August 2020}}</ref> which transmit light to subterranean photosynthetic sites.

''Fenestraria rhopalophylla'' is native to [[Namaqualand]] in southern Africa and to [[Namibia]]. The plants generally grow in sandy or calciferous soils under low < 100 mm rainfall, that occurs in the winter.

==Subspecies==
Two subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
* ''F. rhopalophylla'' subsp. ''rhopalophylla'' – with white flowers in autumn; native to Namibia
* ''F. rhopalophylla'' subsp. ''aurantiaca'' {{small|(N.E.Br.) H.E.K.Hartmann}} (synonym ''F. aurantiaca'' {{small|N.E.Br.}}) – with yellow flowers; native to Namibia and the northwestern Cape Provinces
